title: MZ Looking for something to fix "star" tileset feature issue

posts.author: miezew
posts.body:
((
Note:
I recently switched to MZ, I originally worked with XP for a couple years. While I'm familiar with the basics, a lot of it is new to me so I'm not entirely sure where to begin to look.))
I'm having this issue where the tiles with the "star" setting applied don't layer correctly and often overlap over the player character and events incorrectly.
Here's what it looks like in a test run of my game:
Spoiler:
(screenshots)
(don't mind the mixels, everything aside from the player character is just placeholder)
Basically I'd like for the object to be behind the player from the front, but in front of them when the player is "behind" it.
If it helps at all, my tile size is set to 32x32, and my player character (and other characters) are about two and a half tiles tall on average. So yes, I am working with bigger character assets than the common 32x32 characters, which I know can cause issues like this sometimes.
Are there any solutions or plugins that are recommended to fix this?
I haven't found anything online, but then again, I'm not sure how I would describe my issue as a simple searchable question either. So I'm asking here now.

posts.author: Norintha
posts.body: Depending on how many events you need to control the switch, you can use the change tileset command to swap between two different versions of the tileset, one with the star when the player should be behind the tile, and one regular passability when the player is over the tile.

posts.author: Solar_Flare
posts.body:
I
asked the same question
a few months ago.
I was using MV, but possibly some of the options mentioned there would also work in MZ. The one I ultimately ended up choosing has already been mentioned.
Other than plugins, you could simply choose not to use star tiles for objects larger than 1 tile. Instead, put large objects onto character sheets and place them as stationary events on the map. Unlike tiles, event ordering works as you'd expect without any plugins. This might be the best option if you have only a few of these; it's maybe not great if you have hundreds.
